subject.title: Agent-to-Agent Communication Tools Have Parameter Conflicts

question: For plain `message(action="send")`, should OpenClaw hide poll content fields from the send schema, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: The current code intentionally allows metadata-only schema padding but rejects non-empty poll content fields; changing that boundary affects shared channel delivery semantics across Discord, Telegram, Feishu, and other message-tool channels.

options.title: Action-scope poll schema
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for explicit poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

options.title: Strip on send
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and drop poll fields before delivery, improving send reliability while potentially masking poll-intent mistakes.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields on send and require live evidence before changing the tool contract further.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll schema
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for explicit poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll-guard and schema-consistency work is the strongest history signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
